reply:
Dear Alberto, all, 
Thanks for the discussion during the official offline. At the end of offline session, there was a saying that the Technique 1 part is almost stable. Sorry but there is still one issue that is not clarified or solved from our perspective. 
The bullet e) under technique 1 is still not very clear to us. 
For the bullet e), it seems should be “by adding a term equal to the two-way uplink Doppler between the CRP and the SAN” instead of one-way Doppler. 
First, the logic for the Doppler frequency compensation of Rel-20 UE should be same and aligned with bullet d) the time domain compensation behavior. Since two-way propagation delay (RTT) is compensated in the time domain, then it should be same for the Doppler shift/frequency domain to compensate the two-way frequency offsets. 
For the bullet d), the DL reference time is the DL reception time at UE. Then the Rel-17 UL timing compensation is the RTT (two-way propagation delay). Then if the frequency domain follows the same logic, then the DL reference frequency is the carrier frequency of the DL reception ( = nominal DL frequency – Doppler shifts in DL). The Rel-17 UE behavior for UL compensation is to compensate the two-way Doppler shifts based on the DL (actual) reception carrier frequency. Then the item e) should be “by adding a term of the two-way uplink Doppler between the CRP and the SAN”, i.e. with the Rel-17 UL compensation in frequency domain minus the two-way UL Doppler between the CRP and the SAN. At last, it seems that the Rel-20 UE does not compensate anything in the UL carrier frequency in general, which is similar to the behavior of unmodified UE. The marginal compensation in UL frequency domain is the difference between the actual one-way Doppler shift and the one between CRP and the SAN. 
Based on the illustration in Figure 2 in R1-2610456, “by adding a term equal to the one-way UL Doppler between the CRP and the SAN” is only correct in the condition that the reference frequency is nominal UL carrier frequency. Based on this assumption, the Rel-17 UE behavior is to compensate the UL transmission with one-way Doppler, which is different from the description of the case that DL reception frequency is considered as reference. Though it is the same fact and behavior, but with difference reference frequency assumptions, there would be a one-way Doppler compensation and two-way Doppler compensation. 
Two options can be considered to further clarify this issue. 
Option 1: 
e.	The UE uplink frequency pre-compensation is modified (with respect to the current one as defined by uplinkPrecompensation-r17) by adding a term equal to the one-way  two-way uplink Doppler between the CRP and the SAN, when actual DL reception carrier frequency is considered as the reference frequency for UL compensation.
Option 2: 
e.	The UE uplink frequency pre-compensation is modified (with respect to the current one as defined by uplinkPrecompensation-r17) by adding a term equal to the one-way uplink Doppler between the CRP and the SAN, when the nominal UL carrier frequency is considered as the reference frequency for UL compensation.
Nominal UL carrier frequency is the one that UE determined based on the DL actual reception frequency and estimated DL Doppler shifts based on the UE location and ephemeris information. 
Either option 1 or option 2 can clarify the background and the assumptions of one-way or two-way Doppler shift compensation. Hope this can clarify the issue and smooth the online discussion. 
Best Regards
YI ZHENG
CMCC

author: Lei Zhang (Fujitsu)
reply:
Dear all,
We will have a 20-minute offline session from 3:00 pm, local time.
The following proposals/observations have been prepared for the offline discussion.
10.5.4.4-related
Proposal 7-1-1: To facilitate the progress of AI 10.5.4.4, the following understanding is supported:
*   For a CG-PUSCH that is not immediately activated (Type-2), the first occasion of the CG-PUSCH that is activated by a DCI is considered as DG-PUSCH.
  *   [For a SPS-PDSCH, the first occasion of the SPS-PDSCH that is activated by a DCI is considered as dynamically scheduled PDSCH.]
UL skipping
Proposal 5-1-1 (Version B): Support UL skipping mechanism for DG-PUSCH and CG-PUSCH in 6GR with following observation:
*   To reduce UL transmission latency, the base station may schedule DG-PUSCH without a request from the UE or configure CG-PUSCH resources for the UE, even when the availability of UL data at the UE is unknown to the base station. In such cases, UL skipping serves as a useful mechanism to avoid unnecessary UL transmissions, thereby reducing UE power consumption and potential UL interference.
  *   Note: the observation will be updated in next meeting, if necessary
Observation 5-2-2:
*   In 5G NR, the Rel-15 and Rel-16 UL skipping behaviors regarding UCI multiplexing are not fully aligned.
     *   In Rel-15, when there is no UL data to be transmitted on a granted PUSCH and UCI is to be multiplexed onto the PUSCH, the PUSCH is skipped.
     *   In Rel-16, under the same condition, the PUSCH is not skipped and is transmitted to carry the UCI.
  *   The Rel-15 behavior may leave ambiguity at the base station as to whether the UCI is transmitted on PUCCH or PUSCH, requiring blind detection on both channels and thereby increasing the processing complexity of the base station.
Joint activation/deactivation
Observation 3-2-1: At least for CG-PUSCH configurations that are not immediately activated and are subsequently activated by an activation DCI and SPS-PDSCH configurations
*   The qualitative benefits of joint activation/deactivation of multiple CG-PUSCH configurations or SPS-PDSCH configurations are generally understood. For example,
     *   Reducing [activation/]deactivation signaling overhead, e.g., DCI overhead;
     *   Reducing the latency of activation/deactivation operations.
  *   However, the actual gain depends on the number of CG-PUSCH/SPS-PDSCH configurations that can be simultaneously active, for which no clear RAN2 conclusion is currently available.
  *   However, the qualitative benefits identified in RAN1 are not sufficient to justify the support for joint activation/deactivation of multiple CG-PUSCH configurations or multiple SPS-PDSCH configurations at this stage.
Best regards,
Lei

Dear all, 
The following is to be discussed in our first offline: 
FL Proposal 3-3-2’
There is no concensus in RAN1 to support DL-WUS indicating RACH occasion (RO) adaptation for UEs in RRC_IDLE/RRC_INACTIVE in 6GR system. 
FL Proposal 4-3-1’
For DL-WUS with CSI report for UEs in RRC_CONNECTED in 6GR, RAN1 to support the following for CSI report:
Baseline (implicit gating): Periodic/semi-persistent CSI reporting associated with a C-DRX cycle is performed only if the DL-WUS triggers PDCCH monitoring for that cycle, without additional DL-WUS payload. 
FFS Whether and how the network enables/disables this behavior with RRC configuration
FFS whether the same applies to periodic/semi-persistent SRS and to CSI measurement.
FFS: Early CSI measurement/report before the triggered PDCCH monitoring (implicit or explicit trigger), including for SCells, provided that the UL resources are configured and the consequence of a false alarm (unintended UL transmission) is assessed.
FL Proposal 4-1-1’
For DL-WUS with Cell DTX or Cell DRX operation for UEs in RRC_CONNECTED in 6GR:
The UE is not required to monitor DL-WUS during the configured cell non-active period, i.e. DL-WUS monitoring occasions are within the configured cell DTX active period, and WUS-triggered PDCCH monitoring is restricted to the cell DTX active period.
Cell DTX/DRX configuration and activation/deactivation follow the RAN2 basic principle.
Interaction with Cell DTX and with Cell DRX is studied separately where the impacts differ.
FFS: alignment between UE active time and Cell DTX/DRX configuration.
FFS: Additional DL-WUS monitoring occasions, configured by the network, during the Cell DTX non-active period for latency-sensitive DL traffic.
FL Proposal 3-1-1’
The following is supported in 6GR for DL-WUS indicating SI modification and/or ETWS/CMAS notification for UEs in RRC_IDLE/RRC_INACTIVE:
Select one of the two opitons for the notification:
o   Opt.1: The notification is carried in the short message of the paging PDCCH, and the DL-WUS triggers UE to monitor paging PDCCH.
o   Opt.2: The notification is carried in a DL-WUS signal and is not required to monitor the paging PDCCH for it.
FFS on the aspects below:
o   The DL-WUS is transmitted in group-specific DL-WUS occasion(s) (Alt.1) monitored by group of UEs within the cell or cell-common DL-WUS occasion(s) (Alt.2) monitored by all UEs within the cell.
o   The SI modification and ETWS/CMAS are indicated by separate or common codepoint(s)/bit(s) with or without finer granularity.

Dear all,
I hope we will have a chance to discuss the following observation and proposal around 11:00 a.m, about 30 to 40 minutes. local time.
Please join the discussion if you are interested.
Observation 6-1-3-1: In 5G NR,
*   UL skipping serves as a useful mechanism to avoid unnecessary UL transmissions, thereby reducing UE power consumption and potential UL interference.
  *   The Rel-15 and Rel-16 UL skipping behaviors regarding UCI multiplexing are not fully aligned.
     *   In Rel-15, when there is no UL data to be transmitted on a granted PUSCH, the PUSCH is skipped.
        *   The Rel-15 behavior may leave ambiguity at the base station as to whether the UCI is transmitted on PUCCH or PUSCH, requiring blind detection on both channels and thereby increasing the processing complexity of the base station.
     *   In Rel-16, when there is no UL data to be transmitted on a granted PUSCH and is a UCI to be multiplexed onto the PUSCH, the PUSCH is not skipped is transmitted to carry the UCI.
Proposal 6-1-3-1:
Support an UL skipping mechanism for DG-PUSCH and CG-PUSCH in 6GR, while the detailed skipping rules are subject to further discussion during the WI phase. For example,
*   Details for UCI multiplexing, [including how to resolve the ambiguity between the Rel-15 and Rel-16 UL skipping behaviors].

It would be appreciated that FL can consider it in your next round of update, and companies can check whether we are correctly capturing your results.
Proposal X: Capture the following observations in the TR.
For UL-WUS used for UL data indication of connected UEs, the NES and UE energy impacts reported by the sources are as follows:
·      For DS#1c with BS Cat 1, NES results are provided by 7 sources ([R1-2610886, Huawei], [R1-2609626, Samsung], [R1-2609799, ZTE], [R1-2610672, CEWiT], [R1-2610714, TCL], [R1-2610814, OPPO], [R1-2610788, Ericsson]).
o   6 sources ([R1-2610886, Huawei], [R1-2609626, Samsung], [R1-2609799, ZTE], [R1-2610672, CEWiT], [R1-2610714, TCL], [R1-2610814, OPPO]) observe NES gain of 0.19% to 81.11% compared with a baseline without UL-WUS:
–      [R1-2610886, Huawei] (SSB periodicity of 40 ms, 80 ms and 160 ms): 2% to 49% for UL-WUS with cell DRX (k from 0.5 to 0.99) compared with periodic SR; 4% to 49% for 160 ms, 8% to 31% for 80 ms, 2% to 36% for 40 ms
–      [R1-2609626, Samsung] (SSB periodicity of 20 ms), compared with periodic SR every 10 ms: 7.8% when UL-WUS replaces periodic SR; 17.9% when UL-WUS is used with cell DRX (160 ms cycle / 20 ms active), versus 21.4% for the same cell DRX without UL-WUS, while the mean latency is reduced from 72.5 ms to 12.4 ms with UL-WUS.
–      [R1-2609799, ZTE] (SSB periodicity not stated): 0.19% to 0.73% compared with periodic SR
–      [R1-2610672, CEWiT] (SSB periodicity of 20 ms): 2.0% to 9.2% compared with SR + BSR (UL-WUS indicates the buffer-size level, BS Set 1)
–      [R1-2610714, TCL] (SSB periodicity not stated): 67.90% to 81.11% compared with periodic SR (single-event model)
–      [R1-2610814, OPPO] (BS category not stated; SSB periodicity of 20 ms): 30.93% compared with CG without UL-WUS (UL-WUS every 160 ms indicates with / without UL data for CG every 20 ms)
o   5 of these 6 sources ([R1-2610886, Huawei], [R1-2609626, Samsung], [R1-2610672, CEWiT], [R1-2610714, TCL], [R1-2610814, OPPO]) observe NES gain of 5% or more in at least one configuration.
o   1 source ([R1-2610788, Ericsson]) observes NES loss:
–      [R1-2610788, Ericsson] (SSB periodicity of 40 ms): 23.8% and 15.4% loss compared with periodic SR, with UL-WUS duration of 2.5 slots and 6 slots every 10 ms (Option 2, k = 0.5, x_a = 0.5 and 0.25)
§  For a configuration similar to the 2.5-slot case of [R1-2610788, Ericsson], 1 source ([R1-2610886, Huawei], Case 2-3-7) reports NES gain instead of loss: with SSB periodicity of 40 ms, Set 4 Option 2 with k = 0.5, half of the TRX used for UL-WUS reception (50% TRX for Huawei, x_a = 0.5 for Ericsson), UL-WUS duration of 2.5 slots every 10 ms, and periodic SR of 1 slot every 10 ms as baseline, [R1-2610886, Huawei] reports 2% NES gain (2% to 6% for k from 0.5 to 0.99) whereas [R1-2610788, Ericsson] reports 23.8% NES loss. Other assumptions differ, e.g., TDD pattern (8/2 vs 4/2/4), traffic model (FTP3 vs not stated).
o   1 source ([R1-2610886, Huawei]) evaluates more than one SSB periodicity, and its results show that, for the same UL-WUS configuration, the NES gain increases with the SSB periodicity: for the 5 configurations evaluated at all three periodicities (SR / UL-WUS periodicity of 10 ms, k from 0.5 to 0.99, the NES gain is 4% to 17% for 40 ms, 8% to 31% for 80 ms and 10% to 37% for 160 ms.
·      For DS#1c with BS Cat 2 / Cat 2.1, NES results are provided by 4 sources ([R1-2610714, TCL], [R1-2610187, Lenovo], [R1-2609626, Samsung], [R1-2609799, ZTE]).
o   2 sources ([R1-2610714, TCL], [R1-2610187, Lenovo]) observe NES gain of 8.28% to 50.31%:

–      [R1-2610187, Lenovo] (SSB periodicity not stated): 11.7% for Cat 2.1, for UL-WUS with cell DTX/DRX of 160 ms compared with cell DTX/DRX of 40 ms, while the mean delay is reduced from 24.9 ms to 15.2 ms
o   2 sources ([R1-2609626, Samsung], [R1-2609799, ZTE]) observe marginal NES impact (between 1.4% loss and 0.6% gain):

–      [R1-2609799, ZTE] (Cat 2.1; SSB periodicity not stated): 0.10% to 0.39% gain compared with periodic SR

           *   The UE is expected to be able to receive PDSCH.
           *   The UE is expected to be able to monitor PDCCH on and/or for the carrier.
           *   The UE is expected to be able to perform CSI measurements.
        *   For UL behaviors,
           *   The UE is expected to be able to transmit PUSCH.
           *   The UE is expected to be able to transmit PUCCH .
           *   The UE is expected to be able to transmit SRS.
           *   The UE is expected to be able to transmit PRACH.
        *   Note: This does not imply the DL behaviors and the UL behaviors must be assumed together or can be separated
     *   Deactivated
        *   For DL behaviors,
           *   The UE is not expected to be able to receive PDSCH.
           *   The UE is not expected to be able to monitor PDCCH on or for the carrier.
           *   The UE is not expected to be able to perform CSI measurements.
        *   For UL behaviors,
           *   The UE is not expected to be able to transmit PUSCH.
           *   The UE is not expected to be able to transmit PUCCH.
           *   The UE is not expected to be able to transmit SRS.

  *   Note: Definition of activated/deactivated states and corresponding UE behaviors in Rel-21 6GR specifications are further discussed in WI phase.
  *   Send LS to RAN2 informing this agreement.

For fast enabling/disabling access to additional carriers for 6GR multiple carrier operation in connected mode, further discuss how to achieve fast transition from deactivated state to activated state for a carrier, considering the following:
*   The transition operation is composed of one or more of the following:
